ethnography is a research method that involves the collection and analysis of data from the perspective of a participant observer in order to understand the cultural and social practices of a group or community.

ethnography is a set of research methods that is based on the assumption that human behavior can best be understood by examining it as it is practiced, in its natural context.

the ways that ethnographic methods and the ethnographic imagination are being used in HCI and the ways in which these are being theorized and understood.
the development and application of ethnographic methods and with their interpretation and use in HCI.

the novelty and mystery of ethnographic methods in HCI is due to a combination of factors: the novelty of the methods themselves; their association with non-traditional domains and practices; their association with forms of analysis that are unfamiliar to HCI’s traditional cognitive science roots; and the fact that the epistemological commitments of ethnography have been poorly understood.
ethnographic methods in HCI have often been misunderstood.

we are interested in the design of interactive systems that are sensitive to the needs, values and practices of the people who use them.
ethnography is a method for studying human behavior and culture in a way that is grounded in the everyday experiences of those being studied.

ethnographic approaches are more than just a way of getting at certain kinds of data, but are also ways of understanding and interpreting the world that can be used in a variety of ways in HCI.
ethnographic approaches are not only useful for the study of HCI, but are in some respects indispensable.
